The honest read

Why do teams leave Wufoo?

Wufoo is stable and quick to set up. What moves teams off it is the meter and the age of the builder.

Entries are metered, and overages are billed

Every plan counts entries. Past the limit, paid accounts are charged $0.05 per entry at the end of the billing period. Free accounts have their forms deactivated at 100 instead.

The interface feels dated

The one complaint corroborated across both G2 and Capterra. A 2026 reviewer titled their review "Easy Setup and Integrations, But Feels Outdated and Hurts Completion Rates".

Basics sit behind paid tiers

Conditional logic starts on Starter and payment collection on Professional. The free plan is 5 forms, 100 entries a month, and 10 fields per form.

No AI anywhere in the product

A dozen first-party Wufoo pages mention no AI form generation, and the footer's AI links point to SurveyMonkey instead.

Migration

How do you switch from Wufoo to Formester?

Three steps, and the meter stops the moment you finish.

1

Export your entries

In Wufoo, open each form's Entries screen and export to CSV or Excel. Keep the file somewhere safe, since the free plan carries no file storage.

Time: about five minutes per form.

2

Rebuild the form with AI

Paste your field list into Formester's AI generator or describe the form in a sentence. It drafts the fields, pages, and design in about half a minute, then you re-add your rules.

Input options: plain prompt, pasted question list, or PDF upload.

3

Repoint embeds and payments

Swap the Wufoo embed for Formester's snippet and reconnect Stripe or PayPal. Send one test submission, then retire the old form once the numbers match.

Safety net: nothing counts against a cap while you test.

Honest comparison

When is Wufoo still the better choice?

Formester is not the answer for every team. Three cases where Wufoo is the better call.

You need more than two payment gateways

Wufoo supports eight processors on Professional and above.

  • Stripe, Square, Authorize.Net, PayPal, USAePay, Braintree, FreshBooks, and Chargify
  • Bring your own merchant account on any of them
  • Formester supports Stripe and PayPal

Choose Wufoo when your processor is not Stripe or PayPal

Reporting breadth matters most

Unlimited reports on every tier, including the free plan.

  • A custom report builder with exports available on all plans
  • Google Analytics tracking from the Professional plan
  • Formester ships drop-off analysis and field summaries rather than a report builder

Choose Wufoo when reporting breadth is the requirement

You already run SurveyMonkey

Wufoo and SurveyMonkey share a parent company.

  • Wufoo is owned by SurveyMonkey Inc, with the acquisition announced in April 2011
  • Their own comparison page routes advanced survey needs to SurveyMonkey
  • Formester runs standalone, with its own billing and integrations

Choose Wufoo if SurveyMonkey is already your system of record

Privacy and data ownership

Who owns your form data?

You do. Everything moving through your forms is Customer Data: the prompts you type, the structures the AI drafts, and every response someone submits. Section 4.4 of our Data Processing Addendum bars Formester from using any of it to train AI models, run advertising, or feed analytics and marketing. The Google Gemini integration that drafts forms works inside the same boundary.

Responses travel over TLS, sit encrypted at rest, and payment data carries an extra AES-256 layer through Stripe. Formester is GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA compliant. We are not SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA certified, and the security page says exactly that instead of hinting otherwise. Compensating controls are in place: encryption in transit and at rest, annual third-party penetration testing, enforced 2FA, and encrypted backups.

DPA §4.4 · January 2026
"Formester shall not use Customer Data for purposes of analytics, advertising, marketing, or training of artificial intelligence or machine learning models, except as strictly necessary to provide the Services."

Formester Data Processing Addendum, effective January 2026.
